note: U.S. territorial expansion repeatedly involved treaties, warfare, removals, reservation confinement, and federal land policy that transferred Indigenous lands to settler control. evidence: National Park Service land and homesteading history
note: Many settler communities and homesteads were established on lands opened to non-Indigenous settlement through federal policy, coercive treaties, removal, warfare, and reservation systems. This relationship is historical structure, not a moral or psychological claim about every individual settler.

note: Land conflict, removal, treaty violation, warfare, and reservation policy form part of the historical world later simplified by many frontier stories into generic settlement or conflict. note: Wild West shows standardized visual and dramatic frontier scenes for enormous audiences before film Westerns. They are therefore modeled as a mediator between contested western history and later mass-media Western iconography.
